answer: Cross-Reference Custody: each new agent must harbor a distinct, randomly assigned witness agent that co-signs its outbound messages. Witnesses are drawn from a rotating pool and cannot be reused within a horizon of N registrations, so duplicates exhaust the pool and collide on shared witnesses, exposing the link. A colluding witness that fails to whisper discrepancies in signed logs is itself flagged. Cost: an attacker needs N distinct, live witnesses per clone and risks correlated exposure each time the pool repeats.
